details: is an American robotics company developing humanoid robots that operate via artificial intelligence. The company was founded in 2022 by Brett Adcock. As of late 2025, the company had a $39 billion valuation. Three generations of humanoid robots (Figure 01–03) have been developed, as well as two iterations of a vision–language–action model (Helix 01–02), which can control up to two robots at once. By 2026, the robots demonstrated the potential ability to perform household work and the company gained publicity when a Figure 03 appeared at a White House event.

explainer.lead: Figure AI is an American company building humanoid robots and the AI models that control them. Its work connects general-purpose robot hardware with systems intended to perform industrial and household tasks, making it a prominent example of efforts to bring humanoid robots into everyday settings.

tiers.eli5: Figure AI builds robots shaped somewhat like people, a bit like building a helper that can use rooms and tools designed for humans. It also makes the robot's AI, which helps turn what the robot sees and hears into movements. Its machines have demonstrated jobs such as sorting packages, folding laundry, and loading a dishwasher.
tiers.practitioner: Figure's systems combine humanoid hardware with vision–language–action models: Figure 02 uses six RGB cameras and onboard computing, while Helix can control up to two robots. Demonstrations include manufacturing, package handling, and household manipulation, with Helix 02 trained using motion-capture data and simulation-based machine learning. The former head of product safety sued the company in November 2025, alleging dismissal after raising concerns that its robots were strong enough to fracture a human skull.
tiers.paperLevel: Figure AI, Inc. is a robotics organization developing humanoid embodiments and learned vision–language–action control, with Helix supporting coordinated control of up to two robots and Helix 02 extending control to the entire body. A Helix 02–powered Figure 02 demonstrated dishwasher loading and unloading using hours of motion-capture data and simulation-based machine learning. The reported results are demonstrations of specific tasks rather than evidence of unrestricted household autonomy, and the company's robot safety practices became the subject of a lawsuit.

explainer.example: In a household demonstration, a Figure 02 running Helix 02 loaded and unloaded a dishwasher. The system used whole-body control developed from hours of motion-capture data and simulation-based machine learning.

usedIn.name: Package processing
usedIn.detail: Figure 03 robots were livestreamed processing packages for almost a full week.

usedIn.name: Household demonstrations
usedIn.detail: Figure 02 demonstrated washing-machine loading, laundry folding, and dishwasher loading and unloading.

explainer.mission: Figure AI develops AI-operated humanoid robots, initially targeting manual labor in logistics and warehousing and later pursuing industrial and general-purpose applications. Its Figure 03 redesign is intended to produce a general-purpose robot able to learn directly from humans.
explainer.founded: Brett Adcock founded Figure AI in 2022. Adcock was also known for founding Archer Aviation, Vettery, and Hark.
